description:
FILED s449q (Opus round-7 agent Q), from the #590 probes.  The RESIDUE of #590:
`close` now returns FALSE where perl returns false, and the program survives;
only the DEFINEDNESS of that false differs.

REPRODUCER (needs a write that fails at the OS -- /dev/full is the portable one):

    open(my $fu, '>', "/dev/full") or die;
    print $fu "tiny";                 # buffered, succeeds
    my $c = close $fu;                # the flush fails, ENOSPC
    printf "close=%s\n", (defined $c ? ($c ? 1 : "defined-false") : "undef");

        perl  close=defined-false     ("" -- perl's false is an empty string)
        PCL   close=undef

Same for every other false close (a pipe whose child exited non-zero, a handle
that is not a stream): `%p-close-maybe-pipe` and `%p-close-impl` return CL NIL,
which the box model reads as undef.

WHY IT IS NOT OBVIOUSLY WORTH FIXING: CL NIL as perl's false-and-undef is the
runtime's general convention, not a close-specific slip, so a fix here either
makes ONE builtin inconsistent with the rest of the io family or opens the
question for all of them.  `defined(close $fh)` is also exotic Perl.

IF IT IS DONE: the discriminator is perl's -- a builtin that FAILED returns ""
(defined), a builtin that had no value returns undef -- so the survey is "which
io builtins does perl answer with a defined false", and `print` is NOT one of
them (probed: a failed print returns undef in perl too, and PCL matches).  Bar:
probe close / print / printf / syswrite / seek / binmode / eof for definedness
of their false, then one change per builtin that diverges, with rows in
Pl/t/fileio-02.t.
subject: A false `close` returns undef where perl returns a DEFINED empty string, so `defined(close $fh)` disagrees
